tests.description: No optional packages: Core bootstrap/login, existing PHP/HTTPS sites and local recovery continue
Hub offline or deleted: Core login, sites, backups and updates remain locally manageable
ONE-CLICK INSTALL absent: existing PHP site functions normally
Docker/Podman absent: native free one-click path does not load container runtime
Optional module fails to boot: no request or scheduler crash in Core
No unverified module gets activated from a catalog card
Planned/developing modules never expose executable routes, workers, jobs, migrations or root handlers
Capability resolver detects cycles, conflicts, missing dependencies, major API mismatches
Feature flags checked at server-side action boundary, not only UI
No activation without host plan quota, role, compatibility and signed artifact
Tenant A cannot inspect/configure/activate tenant B modules
Optional module disable retains customer data and does not undo Core migrations
Module-specific upgrade failure restores service or declares controlled recovery
Core update with older/incompatible plugin fails closed without deadlocking startup
Catalog source outage does not block website serving, local auth or backup restore
Unqualified recipe is not installable even if its card is shown
Signed and approved native recipe cannot invoke container engine by fallback
Container app cannot silently convert to native or mount root/engine socket
Module UI status shows truthful SPECIFIED/DEVELOPING/VERIFIED evidence labels
Admin preview visibility does not grant install or RBAC permissions
FR/EN module descriptions and fallback rendered without XSS or broken empty routes
Unsupported OS/WebStack is not offered as certified regardless of roadmap target
Effective user actions remain audited, secrets redacted, MFA optional
Backup and actual isolated restore succeed for all shipped essential data
One critical P0/P1 issue blocks GA even if optional work is postponed
RC freeze excludes unfinished optional features from signed artifact
Signed package provenance, digest and exact commit match release manifest
Incremental patch releases backport security on all declared maintained branches
Hub premium failure never denies AGPL free Core or deletes existing sites
Private Hub release and keys never bundled into public Core artifact
No simulated timestamp, scripted output or documentation CI claims operating system certification
Core tested live via Symfony HTTP + PG concurrent transactions before R3 install authority
First OS/WebStack chosen only after comparative VM, security, recovery evidence
Public beta remains blocked until licensing/CLA/security channels and privacy readiness complete
PR required for features→develop and signed tag on main, production branch does not confer deploy status
